name: International Protection (Refugee Status / Subsidiary Protection)

qualifying_event.description: The General Department of Immigration (Ministry of Home Affairs) decides on applications for international protection. Applicants express their wish to apply at the Ministry, airport control, Grand-Ducal Police, or detention facilities, then register at the General Department of Immigration.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Registration ('pink document'); in-depth interview; supporting documents.

requirements.blocker_text: The General Department of Immigration assesses eligibility for refugee status or subsidiary protection following an in-depth interview. Normal procedure: 6-month standard response, capped at 21 months. Accelerated procedure (safe-country origin, false information, or contradicted statements): typically 2 months.
Must register the application in person and receive the 'pink document' certificate (issued ~3 days after submission, valid 1 month, renewable monthly) permitting stay during processing.

evidence_required.document: Grounds for protection presented at interview, with supporting documents

outcome.duration_length: 5-year residence permit for both refugee status and subsidiary protection

sources.title: Guichet.lu -- Applying for International Protection: General Department of Immigration process, registration, interview, 6-month (max 21-month) normal timeline, 2-month accelerated procedure
Guichet.lu -- Rights Conferred by International Protection: 5-year residence permit for both refugee and subsidiary protection statuses, full work rights, education/healthcare parity with citizens

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Luxembourg). Unusually strong tier-1 sourcing for this category compared to several other international_protection.json builds in this dataset (which often rely on tier-2 UNHCR or tier-3/4 NGO sourcing) -- both the process and the outcome durations are confirmed directly on guichet.lu. Refugee status and subsidiary protection receive the SAME 5-year permit duration in Luxembourg, unlike several other countries in this dataset (e.g. Sweden, Finland) where subsidiary protection gets a shorter permit than refugee status. citizenship_after_months (60) uses lu_naturalisation.json's standard 5-year bar; protected persons also separately qualify for the 'acquisition by option' route (case 9 of 10, per lu_naturalisation.json's notes) after 5 years, language test, and civics course -- not modeled as a distinct file, consistent with this dataset's practice of not building a separate route for every one of Luxembourg's 10 option sub-cases.
